title: In Vitro Multiparametric Cellular Analysis by Micro Organic Charge-modulated Field-effect Transistor Arrays
protocol: Prepare the developing solution by diluting NaOH pellets in deionized water at a concentration of 175 mM.
Prepare the titanium etching solution by diluting hydrofluoric acid (HF) in deionized water at a ratio of 1 part HF to 49 parts deionized water.
Prepare the gold etching solution by mixing iodine, potassium iodide, and deionized water for a total of 250 g solution. Use 200 mL of deionized water, 20 g of KI, and 5 g of I2.
Stir the gold etching solution at room temperature for 1 h.
Leave the gold etching solution resting overnight before use.
Dissolve 6,13-bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl) pentacene (TIPS Pentacene) in anisole (1% in weight).
Gently stir the semiconductor solution for 2 h on a hot plate at 80 °C.
Cut a 6 x 6 cm² square of 250 µm polyethylene terephthalate (PET) from a pristine PET sheet.
Inspect the substrate with an optical microscope.
Exclude substrates with deep grooves and scratches.
Rinse PET substrates with acetone, isopropyl alcohol, and deionized water in sequence.
Dry the substrates using nitrogen streams.
Store the substrates in clean plastic Petri dishes/containers.
Pre-clean the substrates with plasma oxygen (30 s at 100 W).
Place the pre-cleaned substrates on the substrate holder inside the vacuum chamber of the thermal evaporator.
Place 60 mg of titanium in the crucible and close the shutter.
Pump down the evaporation chamber until it reaches a vacuum level lower than 10-6 Torr.
Increase the power of the evaporator until the crucible glows red.
Wait for 30 s, then open the shutter.
Increase the power to 60% (or until the crucible glows bright white) and wait for 60 s.
Close the shutter and turn down the power.
Remove the substrates from the evaporator.
Clean the substrates using acetone, isopropyl alcohol, and deionized water.
Dry the cleaned substrates using nitrogen streams.
Perform a second oxygen plasma treatment (60 s at 200 W) to slightly oxidize the titanium surface.
Place one substrate at a time on the spin coater inside a fume hood.
Deposit 4 mL of photoresist on the substrate using a disposable plastic pipette.
Spin coat the photoresist at 3000 rpm for 45 seconds with an acceleration and deceleration time of 0.5 seconds each to obtain a 2 µm-thick layer.
Soft bake the photoresist by placing the substrate on a hot plate at 70 °C for 5 minutes.
Store the substrate inside an aluminum foil-wrapped Petri dish or plastic container to avoid direct light exposure.
Position the photolithographic mask with the desired FG layout onto the substrate in the bromograph.
Expose the substrate to ultraviolet (UV) light from the top for 1 minute.
Carefully remove the mask, taking care to minimize lateral movements over the substrate to avoid scratching it.
Plunge the substrate for 5 seconds into a glass container filled with developing solution.
Quickly rinse the substrate in deionized water and dry it under nitrogen.
Use an optical microscope to look for underdeveloped or overdeveloped spots in the substrate.
Repeat immersion of the substrate in developing solution if necessary due to underdevelopment.
Etch the exposed titanium by submerging it in the titanium etching solution for 15 s.
Rinse the substrate with deionized water.
Dry the substrate using nitrogen.
Remove the photoresist using acetone.
Rinse the substrate with isopropyl alcohol.
Rinse the substrate with deionized water.
Dry the substrate with nitrogen.
Distribute 2 mL of silane on the deposition chamber walls using a laboratory wipe.
Place 300 mg of Parylene C dimer onto the Parylene coater.
Set the lower pressure value to 7 mbar.
Set the higher pressure value to 10 mbar.
Clean the substrates with acetone after deposition.
Clean the substrates with isopropyl alcohol.
Clean the substrates with deionized water.
Dry the substrates with nitrogen.
Deposit the photoresist on the substrates using the same parameters as steps 4.1 and 4.2.
Position the plastic photolithographic mask onto the substrate for the vias under a stereoscopic microscope.
Expose to UV light from the top for 1 min.
Carefully remove the mask, taking care to minimize lateral movements over the substrate.
Develop the photoresist as previously described in step 4.4.
Expose the substrate with the patterned photoresist to oxygen plasma (180 s at 200 W).
Remove the Parylene C from the sensing areas using oxygen plasma.
Place substrates into a glass container filled with acetone inside an ultrasonic bath for 10 seconds.
Rinse substrates with acetone.
Rinse substrates with isopropyl alcohol.
Rinse substrates with water.
Dry substrates with nitrogen.
Deposit photoresist on the substrates using the same parameters as steps 4.1 and 4.2.
Place device in a bromograph.
Position plastic photolithographic mask with black rectangles covering transistor areas onto substrate.
Expose to UV light for 1 minute from both top and bottom.
Carefully remove mask, minimizing lateral movements over substrate.
Develop photoresist as previously described in step 4.4.
Clean the substrates with a gentle plasma treatment (30 s at 30 W).
Place the cleaned substrates on the holder inside the vacuum chamber of the thermal evaporator.
Place 30 mg of gold in the crucible and close the shutter.
Pump down the evaporation chamber until it reaches 10-5 Torr.
Increase the power of the evaporator until the crucible glows red, wait for 30 s.
Open the shutter and increase the power to 40% (or until the crucible glows bright white).
Wait for 60 s with the shutter open at 40% power.
Close the shutter and turn down the power.
Place substrates into an acetone container inside the ultrasonic bath for 10 s.
Rinse the substrates with acetone, isopropyl alcohol, and water.
Dry the substrates with nitrogen.
Deposit photoresist on the substrates using the same parameters of steps 4.1 and 4.2.
Place the device in a bromograph.
Position a plastic photolithographic mask with desired layout onto the substrate.
Expose to UV light for 1 min from the top.
Carefully remove the mask, minimizing lateral movements over the substrate to avoid scratching it.
Develop the photoresist as described in step 4.4.
Etch the exposed gold by submerging it in the gold etching solution for 10 s.
Rinse the substrate with deionized water.
Dry the substrate using nitrogen.
Remove the photoresist using acetone.
Rinse the substrate with isopropyl alcohol.
Rinse the substrate with deionized water.
Dry the substrate with nitrogen.
Deposit the photoresist on the substrates using the same parameters of steps 4.1 and 4.2.
Position a plastic photolithographic mask onto the substrate, covering the pH-sensing areas.
Expose to UV light for 1 min from the top.
Carefully remove the mask.
Develop the photoresist as described in step 4.4.
Protect the whole device, except for the pH-sensing areas, with polyimide insulation tape.
Deposit a layer of 500 nm of Parylene C on the substrate using the same parameters described in step 5.1.
Carefully remove the polyimide insulation tape.
Expose the substrate to oxygen plasma (5 min and 30 s at 200 W) to activate the Parylene C on the pH-sensing areas of the OCMFETs.
Place the substrates into an acetone container inside the ultrasonic bath for 10 s to completely remove the photoresist.
Rinse the substrates with acetone and isopropyl alcohol (no water) and dry them with nitrogen.
Place the substrates onto a hot plate at 50 °C.
Cast a droplet (1 µL) of semiconductor solution onto each channel area.
Cover the whole substrate with a lid and let it dry out under a chemical hood for 30 min.
Print an acrylonitrile butadiene styrene ring with an internal radius of 15 mm, a thickness of 1 mm, and a height of 7 mm with a 3D printer.
Glue the culturing chamber onto the central part of the substrate using polydimethylsiloxane (ratio of the curing agent: 15% by weight).
Cut out the device from the PET either manually or using a laser cutter.
